title: Name and Classify Haloalkanes: NCERT Questions Solved
subject: Chemistry
objective: Three NCERT exercise questions solved with one checklist: longest chain (look inside the branches), lowest locants, alphabetical order on a tie; and the class (1°, 2°, 3°) is decided only by the carbon that carries the halogen. CH₃CH₂C(CH₃)₂CH₂I is 1-iodo-2,2-dimethylbutane (1°), CH₃C(Cl)(C₂H₅)CH₂CH₃ is 3-chloro-3-methylpentane (3°), and CH₃CH(Cl)CH(Br)CH₃ is 2-bromo-3-chlorobutane.

fill.q: The class (1°, 2°, 3°) of an alkyl halide is decided by the carbon that carries the ____.
A carbon bonded to three other carbons makes a ____ alkyl halide when it carries X.
If both ends give the same locants, ____ order decides the lower number.
The longest chain may run through a group written as C₂H₅, which adds ____ carbons.
CH₃CH(Cl)CH(Br)CH₃ has two halogens, so it is a ____ compound.

tf.q: CH₃CH₂C(CH₃)₂CH₂I is a tertiary alkyl halide.
tf.explain: The C–I carbon is bonded to one carbon: primary.

tf.q: The parent chain of CH₃C(Cl)(C₂H₅)CH₂CH₃ is pentane.
tf.explain: The chain runs through the ethyl group: 5 carbons.

tf.q: Alphabetical order is applied before the lowest-locant rule.

tf.explain: The C–Br carbon is bonded to three carbons.

ar.a: Assertion: CH₃CH₂C(CH₃)₂CH₂I is a primary alkyl halide. Reason: The class depends only on the carbon that carries the halogen.
ar.r: Both true; the reason explains the assertion.

ar.a: Assertion: CH₃CH(Cl)CH(Br)CH₃ is named 2-chloro-3-bromobutane. Reason: When locants tie, the prefix first in alphabetical order gets the lower number.

mcq.q: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂C(CH₃)₂CH₂I is:
The IUPAC name of CH₃C(Cl)(C₂H₅)CH₂CH₃ is:
The IUPAC name of CH₃CH(Cl)CH(Br)CH₃ is:

mcq.explain: Br on the sp³ carbon next to C=C.

num.q: Number of carbons in the parent chain of CH₃C(Cl)(C₂H₅)CH₂CH₃.
Number of carbons bonded to the C–Cl carbon in 3-chloro-3-methylpentane.

short.q: Give the IUPAC name and class of (CH₃)₂CHCH(Cl)CH₃ (NCERT Ex 6.1 i).
Give the IUPAC name and class of CH₃C(C₂H₅)₂CH₂Br (NCERT Ex 6.1 vi).
Classify p-ClC₆H₄CH₂CH(CH₃)₂ and m-ClCH₂C₆H₄CH₂C(CH₃)₃ (NCERT Ex 6.1 x, xi).
short.solution: Aryl halide (Cl on the ring); primary benzyl halide (Cl on a CH₂ attached to the ring).

short.q: Write the four C₄H₉Br isomers and classify each (NCERT Ex 6.6).

short.solution: From the I end the locants are 1,2,2, lower than 4,3,3.

match.explain: Each NCERT structure with its IUPAC name.
